patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — ServiceM8 and Contractor Foreman share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose ServiceM8 only if your buying job matches “Field service management for trades — scheduling, dispatch, quotes, and invoicing.” rather than Contractor Foreman's shape. Choose Contractor Foreman only if your buying job matches “Construction management software for contractors — affiliate partner in project management” rather than ServiceM8's shape. Workflow advantage: ServiceM8 leans trades-field-service; Contractor Foreman leans construction-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — ServiceM8 and Contractor Foreman share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: ServiceM8 is Field service management for trades — scheduling, dispatch, quotes, and invoicing.; Contractor Foreman is Construction management software for contractors — affiliate partner in project management..
- Workflow coverage skew: ServiceM8-leaning trades-field-service vs Contractor Foreman-leaning construction-management.
- Researched limits: ServiceM8 — Field service/trades scope — not general PM; Contractor Foreman — Construction vertical — not general PM.

Limitations — ServiceM8: Field service/trades scope — not general PM; Contractor Foreman: Construction vertical — not general PM.

Poor-fit cases: ServiceM8 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Field service/trades scope — not general PM · Contractor Foreman is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Construction vertical — not general PM · Avoid ServiceM8 if you actually need Contractor Foreman's motion (Construction management software for contractors — affiliate partner in project )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
